source: we found that 77% of schools’ policies specifically prohibit the visibility of certain body parts.
claim: 373 of the 481 schools prohibit the visibility of at least one body part.

source: The Most Commonly Banned Visible Body Parts
claim: The body parts most commonly banned are midsection midriff in 340 schools (71%), cleavage in 106 (22%), back in 74 (15%), breasts chest in 69 (14%), buttocks in 54 (11%), shoulders in 38 (8%) and torso in 33 (7%).

source: I was expecting something like genitals to be number one, but only 6 schools (1%) explicitly ban them.
The average dress code prohibits around 32 items (the maximum was 97).
claim: Dress codes list an average of 31.48 rules per school, with a maximum of 97.

source: we found 15% of schools that prohibited items specifically for either “male” students or “female” students
claim: 70 of the 481 schools prohibit at least one item only for male or only for female students.

source: Most Common Words in the Rationale for Dress Codes
claim: The ten most common rationale phrases appear in 367 schools (76%) for disruption/distraction, 330 (69%) for appropriate/inappropriate, 315 (65%) for safe/safety, 184 (38%) for health, 151 (31%) for interfere with learning, 146 (30%) for clean, 97 (20%) for neat, 90 (19%) for modest/modesty, 61 (13%) for respect/disrespect and 48 (10%) for good taste.

source: You’ll find short shorts and skirts at the highest end alongside visible underwear.
claim: The clothing items banned in the most schools are short shorts (334 schools), the undergarment item visible (332) and short skirts (290).

source: On the opposite end, you’ll find items banned in fewer schools like spandex clothing, gym shorts, and the absence of underwear.
claim: At the other end, spandex is banned in 41 schools, the undergarment item none in 32 and athletic gym shorts in 24.

source: Another 33% didn’t specify a length, just prohibited “short” items of clothing.
claim: The "short"/"inappropriate length" (no exact measurement given) category has 159 entries, equal to 33% of the 481 schools.
